page: Amazon Web Services c8i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The dedicated CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and is supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression at 34.45 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.45 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Geekbench single-core testing also registers in the top 25% with a score of 2211.0, while text processing performance reaches the top 10% at 2952.0. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 17296.91 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 13253.0, both falling within the average range. The instance also demonstrates top-tier performance in small-model LLM text generation, achieving 348.03 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8i.4xlarge offers a dense compute profile with DDR5 memory speeds, though the lack of local storage requires external network-attached storage, which may impact overall I/O costs. Network bandwidth is limited to an 8 Gbps baseline. This instance is suited for compute-heavy workloads such as text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, software compilation, and small-scale language model inference.
